questions.prompt: What should the first /goal execution of this SAAS lane prioritize?
questions.description: Lane ownership is fixed (node/saas + saas-starter only; COORD for contracts). This picks the first concrete work bar inside that boundary.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Baseline health + coherence pass: fix broken Jinja gates, shared package/lib collisions, and layering inconsistencies under owned paths; emit COORD handoffs for any contract gaps. Defer broad feature expansion until the tree is coherent.

options.label: Baseline coherence
options.description: Health pass on gates, layering, package/lib collisions; COORD handoffs only for contract gaps

options.label: Combination hardening
options.description: Drive validate_saas_combinations + sample-matrix coherence; fix failures under owned paths

options.label: Stack depth (one vertical)
options.description: Deepen one popular stack (e.g. Next+Vercel+Neon+Clerk+Stripe) end-to-end under owned paths

options.label: Full module sweep
options.description: Broader pass across runtime → integrations → UI → compliance in one execution

questions.prompt: For large SAAS work, which internal sequencing should the plan enforce?
questions.description: Still one ownership boundary (shared package.json / lib collisions). Sequencing only — not separate write lanes unless you later split.
questions.recommendedAnswer: runtime → hosting/ORM/db wiring → auth → billing → remaining integrations → UI/marketing → compliance/observability/tests. Always resolve shared package/lib collisions before parallelizing sub-areas.

options.label: Canonical layers
options.description: runtime → infra wiring → auth → billing → integrations → UI → compliance

options.label: Sample-first
options.description: Start from saas-starter sample failures and walk inward

options.label: Collision-first
options.description: Audit shared package.json / lib roots first, then modules

questions.prompt: How deep should automated verification go for this goal?
questions.description: Render hand-edits remain forbidden. PLATFORM owns sample answers; SAAS may only validate against existing answers files.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Standard: riso validate on representative saas-starter variants + validate_saas_combinations when available + validate_jinja_templates scoped or full when available. No sample render hand-edits; note COORD/PLATFORM handoffs if answers/matrix need changes.

options.label: Strict matrix
options.description: All saas-starter variants validate + combination script; flag every failure

questions.prompt: How should SAAS request Copier/contract changes from COORD?
questions.description: SAAS must not edit copier.yml, hooks, macros, or module_catalog.json.jinja.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Write a short COORD handoff note under goals/riso-lane-saas/handoffs/ with: need, proposed saas_* keys/when-conditions, affected samples, and verification. Do not edit contract files from this lane.

options.label: Inline in plan only
options.description: List COORD asks in plan.md risks; no separate files

options.label: COORD goal package
options.description: File requests into goals/riso-lane-coord/ when that package exists

questions.prompt: Any known SAAS pain points or must-not-break surfaces for this first execution?
questions.description: Optional. Leave blank to discover from codebase. Prefer concrete paths, modules, or sample variants.
questions.recommendedAnswer: None predetermined — discover via validate scripts and layered when-conditions. Must not break: non-SaaS node trees outside node/saas/; layering saas_infra → auth → billing; existing saas-starter variant answers (PLATFORM-owned).
